criteria.criterion: A project whose config declares no overrides syncs byte-for-identical to today's behavior — verified by the existing reconciler suite passing unchanged and a test asserting the composed default map equals the current hardcoded constants.
A per-project overlay changes only the keys it names, layering over the default block which layers over the built-in default — verified by a config-effect contrast test.
Every mapping axis (status, type, link relation, priority) is driven by the config seam rather than a hardcoded literal, with the built-in default as fallback.
A rebar type with no target analogue can be collapsed (round-trip-safe via a rebar-type: label) or skipped (whole-ticket), and an unmapped-non-skipped type fails closed at config load.

A non-allowed transition is attempted by replay of rebar's recorded hops and, failing that (or when no recorded trail survives, e.g. a compacted ticket), drifts — never restricting rebar's local transitions.
A non-representable parent drifts and leaves an echo-safe breadcrumb naming the nearest represented ancestor's Jira key.
Required-field create failures are prevented by a per-project create_defaults block.
A rebar bridge suggest-mapping command interrogates a live target and emits suggested config for every offline-discoverable axis, flagging transitions as best-effort.
rebar doctor detects Jira-compat config problems (offline validation failures and live-drift against the target).

The mapping core is provider-neutral: the schema, layered merge, validation, application semantics, and capability descriptor contain no Jira-specific literal; Jira specifics live only in the adapter.
